current_prose.html: After exact trace reproduction, we compare paired loss differences using Diebold–Mariano (1995) statistics with Bartlett Newey–West (1987) covariance. The fixed bandwidth is L=max{H,⌊4(n/100)<super>2/9</super>⌋}; doubled bandwidth supplies a sensitivity check. Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold (1997) supply the reported small-sample multiplier, here used as an approximation for pinball loss. Fixed finite estimation windows motivate the unconditional predictive-ability interpretation of Giacomini and White (2006), under mixing, adequate high-order moments and positive long-run variance. Shared training can extend dependence beyond the target horizon. These are working assumptions for this post-result analysis.

requirements.scope_limit: No paired losses, HAC long-run variance or reference probabilities were recalculated here. Fixed-window unconditional CPA interpretation is explained, not its empirical assumptions proven; shared training can require dependence bandwidth beyond H. HLN applied to pinball is explicitly approximate.

current_prose.html: Kupiec (1995) proportion-of-failures and Christoffersen (1998) independence/conditional-coverage diagnostics use the original first-origin-plus-j(H+1) grid. Conditional coverage here adds full-sample-grid POF to the transition-independence LR. A DQ-type full-sample HAC Wald adaptation of Engle and Manganelli (2004) uses the intercept, issue-known capacity and matured hit lags H+1 through H+4. Singular covariance or an unidentified transition row yields NA. The fixed 72-member common-history family receives Holm (1979) adjustment; exact identical losses use conservative p=1 solely for multiplicity bookkeeping. Appendix H and the output CSVs retain all statistics and statuses.

current_prose.section: Appendix H. Complete post-result inference and specification outputs
current_prose.html: The HAC covariance uses centered moment products with denominator n. DQ instruments are the intercept, four matured hit lags and standardized issue-known capacity; its chi-square reference has six degrees of freedom when full rank. The covariance must be finite, full rank and positive definite. The doubled bandwidth remains much shorter than the longest training history, so this limited check does not establish adequate long-run covariance calibration. Sparse grid tests remove overlapping target windows but retain shared training dependence. Treasury grid sizes of 40 or12 are particularly weak for asymptotic reference calibration. The equality-based POF, CC and DQ diagnostics require exact 5% moments; a quantile with atoms can validly be conservative, so rejection by low hit frequency differs from undercoverage. Missing transition-state rows render independence and CC unidentified. HLN was derived for mean-squared-error comparisons; pinball p values are approximate. Holm familywise control requires valid component p values: the adjustment does not validate the working DM references or remove post-inspection selection. All analyses are post-result and reuse inspected samples.

current_prose.section: Appendix H. Complete post-result inference and specification outputs
current_prose.html: The DQ-type null is E[Z<sub>t</sub>(I<sub>t</sub>−.05)]=0 for the six raw instruments: the intercept, four mature hit lags and issued capacity. The implementation centers/scales capacity across diagnostic rows for numerical conditioning. With the intercept and a finite positive capacity standard deviation, this common invertible column transformation leaves the Wald statistic unchanged in exact arithmetic. Its sample constants are not forecast inputs or claimed available at issue. Rejection concerns these moments; nonrejection leaves other conditional departures untested. The original out-of-sample CAViaR theorem assumes growing estimation and evaluation samples with their evaluation-to-estimation ratio tending to zero. The fixed-window, overlapping-target HAC calculation here is an adaptation, not a direct application of that theorem.

requirements.partial_or_not_literal: The implemented DQ is not the original one-step CAViaR out-of-sample DQ statistic/theorem. It is an explicitly named HAC conditional-moment adaptation for overlapping targets and fixed estimation windows. This is a methodological adaptation rather than literal original-formula compliance.
requirements.scope_limit: The sparse grids remove target overlap, not common-estimation dependence. POF/CC/DQ equality moments require exactly 5% strict hits; a valid quantile with a floor atom can be conservative. Small Treasury grids and boundary rows limit chi-square calibration. Nonrejection is not conditional calibration.

requirements.requirement:
- **C1 在 Discussion 中正面分析最可能的机制。** Treasury 直接沿用了为小时级 FX 设计的 33 维特征，导致：
  - 25 个滞后水平放在周数据上，等于用了 24 周的水平值；
  - hour-of-day 的正余弦在周三收盘数据上是常数；
  - W=52 时，34 个参数只配 52 个重叠样本，明显过参数化；
  - Treasury 四个格子的 λ 全部落在菜单端点。

current_prose.html: The executed QR specifications perform poorly on the weekly Treasury task. Their 25 level coordinates span the current observation through 24 weeks of history. The two hour coordinates, two weekday coordinates and gap indicator are exactly constant on this weekly source. Training-only centering makes those five columns exactly zero, so they provide no predictive variation and are not a demonstrated mechanism of overfitting. The original nominal design has 33 predictors plus an intercept, or 34 coefficients, with at most 28 varying columns and 29 potentially predictive coefficients before other collinearity, against W=52 overlapping training labels in the shorter history. All four Treasury penalty selections are menu endpoints. Its 52 validation origins contain at most 3 disjoint H24 label paths, a path count rather than an effective-sample-size estimate. Correlated lag levels, overlapping labels, restricted tuning, target dynamics and reporting composition remain competing explanations. Neither the parsimonious sensitivity nor the aggregate panel separates those mechanisms.

evidence: conditional_features.py:35–65 specifies 25 current/lagged levels and 33 total coordinates; 68–79 centers exact constant columns to zero.
treasury-feature-audit.json reports all five constant coordinates 28–32 and the weekly clock, 52 short-window labels and four original endpoint selections.
Current Discussion distinguishes nominal34 coefficients from at most29 potentially varying coefficients before other collinearity.
requirements.not_proven: The plan's diagnosis that constant hourly coordinates cause overfitting and that the design is demonstrably overparameterized is not established by these facts. Constant centered columns cannot themselves add predictive variation. Feature/lag dependence, short validation, target dynamics, tuning bounds and reporting composition remain competing explanations.
requirements.disposition: The current qualified discussion is more defensible than asserting the plan's causal conjecture as fact. No new fitting is needed or authorized by this audit to manufacture such a conclusion.

current_prose.html: The four-predictor sensitivity uses B, signed N and short/long increment RMS, with validation penalties {0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10}. It lowers loss against the original QR in 5 of 8 cells and against matched F in 3 cells. In the Treasury primary cell its loss change is -32.2% relative to the original QR and 2.17% relative to F. All adverse cells remain in Table 8. The exercise changes features and the penalty menu jointly, so it measures a parsimonious specification sensitivity rather than identifying a feature-only cause or rehabilitating the original primary.

A post-result / exploratory selected-fit readback examines the Treasury C2 menu boundary directly (Appendix I). At λ=10, standardized response-normalized slope norms range from 0.001497 to 0.01937. Removing slopes while keeping each fitted intercept changes capacity by a mean absolute 136.8–832.3 source USD millions across the four cells. Relative to the lower empirical headroom-quantile report I, observed loss is 0.2432–2.192% lower; this descriptive difference has no dedicated selection-adjusted test. The fits have small normalized slopes and high headroom correlation with I, but are not identical to I or F. A boundary penalty and high capacity correlation do not by themselves demonstrate zero feature value. Three of the four C2 cells still have higher loss than F.
